title: Redwood All-Hands - October 2026 Leadership Update
summary: Leadership reviewed Q3 results, progress on Dedicated and Private launches, and roadmap priorities for Q4. Key asks: baseline benchmarking for large customers, finalize rollout plan for regional private deployments, and hiring for infra and customer ops. Session ended with open Q&A and several action items captured.
topics: Operational focus: reliability, fallbacks, cost controls
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: leadership + all employees (internal all-hands)
Notes: deck shared (link: internal/redwood/oct-2026-all-hands.pdf)

[00:00] Samira (CEO): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you carving time out on a tuesday. quick agenda — high level metrics, a few product spotlights, org updates, and then q and a. uh lina will kick off with product.

[00:32] Lina (VP Product): thanks samira, okay, page two — quick reminder: our north star this quarter was throughput per dollar for real customer workloads. we've seen a 14% improvement in hosted unit economics month-over-month, driven mostly by smarter batching and prefix cache improvements. there are still edge cases where latency spikes, especially on long chat sessions.

[01:05] Ethan (CTO): yep and to add, the runtime team landed the new kernel selector for transformer-xx models; that cut median p99 by about 20% on A100s in our internal bench, though on some quantized paths there's some jitter — we think that's a kernel scheduling mismatch, we're tracking it. note: the bench doc is in the shared folder, it's called 'kernels-v2-bench-2026-10'.

[01:38] Priya (Head of Eng): small clarification, the jitter shows up mostly when we fall back between on-chip quantized kernels and fp16 paths; the KV cache evictions cause extra copies. sometimes the transcription recorded it as K-V cash, so just fyi, that's a mis-heard term.

[02:10] Samira: thanks priya, good color. michael, quick finance update?

[02:20] Michael (CFO): sure. headline: ARR grew 28% year-over-year this quarter. ARR is a hair under plan because a couple of large renewals slipped a week, but expansion revenue is healthy. gross margin is improving as we push more workloads to optimized instances and the Ded — sorry 'Dedicated' commit uptake is higher than forecast. cost sensitivity is still top-of-mind for mid-market buyers.

[03:00] Jordan (Head CS): customer wins — we announced three mid-market customers on Dedicated, two private pilots in EMEA, and a big POC with a healthcare company that's very focused on audit logs and data residency. security asked us to prioritize the audit-log export feature for private deployments.

[03:35] Samira: great. alex, research highlights?

[03:40] Alex (Head of Research): we've been focusing on model variants for latency fallbacks — smaller models that maintain quality with quantization. the optimize team shipped a recommendations engine that suggests quantization profiles based on real workload distributions. there are occasional mis-labels in the UI where 'quantization profile' shows up as 'quantize profile' — we'll patch that.

[04:15] Lina: product roadmap — rolling items for Q4: 1) general availability of regional Private control plane (EMEA + APAC pilot), 2) Redwood Optimize v1.2 with workload-aware batching suggestions, 3) improved observability in the console (per-route tracing hooks). target dates are in the deck.

[04:50] Priya: engineering priorities to make those dates: finish autoscaler for Dedicated by 11/10, complete private control plane GA by 11/30, and a reliability sprint focused on p99 regressions starting next week. we'll need two more infra hires and one senior SRE.

[05:25] Samira: hiring — we're greenlighting three headcount reqs for infra and two for customer ops. hiring ramp is slower in some regions; recruiting is working with hiring managers to prioritize.

[06:00] Michael: quick on bookings: we're seeing longer sales cycles for Private deals given procurement and legal timelines, expect deal slip risk but higher ACV when they close.

[06:25] Jordan: on CS ops, we noted a pattern: top customers want baseline benchmarks run against their LLM prompts. SEs, please coordinate benchmarks and we'll offer a dedicated bench sprint.

[06:45] Ethan: technical note — the smart routing layer now supports policy-based fallbacks: latency-first, cost-first, and region-first. there was a small bug where the region-first policy didn't respect model version pinning; that's fixed in staging. also a reminder: when we say 'KV cache' in docs some transcripts read 'K V cash' so our internal search may not index correctly.

[07:20] Employee Q (Engineering): curious about model rollouts — can we get a canary window metric in the console?

[07:30] Lina: yes, that's on the roadmap for observability. we'll add a per-rollout canary metric and a health-check breakdown.

[08:00] Employee (Sales): any changes to pricing or credits for Dedicated pilots?

[08:10] Michael: no list price changes this quarter. for pilots we can offer credits, and sales should coordinate with finance for non-standard discounts. we'll post a pilot credit guideline doc.

[08:45] Samira: security & compliance update — emily in security couldn't join but sent notes: SOC 2 Type II audit prep is on track, ISO intake started for some enterprise customers, KMS integration for Private is in final testing. highlight: audit logs export for private deployments prioritized as Jordan said.

[09:20] Priya: ops item — we want to standardize fallback policies for customers by workload type; SEs will help classify. this reduces cognitive load for customers and helps us tune batching.

[09:55] Alex: research request — we need labeled prompt sets across customers to measure quality regressions when changing kernels/quantization. SEs and CS to help gather anonymized prompt sets.

[10:25] Samira: okay, shoutouts — great work on the kernels release and the Optimize recommendation engine. special shout to the infra on the autoscaler POC.

[10:50] Open Q&A — mixed questions from product, eng, sales.

[11:05] Employee (Customer Success): is there a public timeline for Private GA?

[11:12] Priya: target GA for regional Private control plane is 11/30, but we'll run pilot customers through Nov. exact dates in the deck, but we'll communicate more strictly next week.

[11:40] Employee (Legal): any updates on standard terms for Private?

[11:45] Michael: legal is templating terms now; procurement-led customers will still need SOWs for on-prem packages.

[12:05] Employee (Engineering): regarding reliability sprint — will there be a blackout window for cumulative deploys?

[12:12] Priya: no planned blackout, but we'll coordinate windows with teams. core infra will run rolling deploys with canaries.

[12:40] Samira: okay, let's do a quick recap and next steps.

[12:50] Samira (recap): 1) SEs to coordinate baseline benchmarks for top customers (Jordan/SEs). 2) infra to finalize autoscaler and private GA dates (Priya). 3) security to prioritize audit-log export (Security). 4) research/CS to collect anonymized prompt sets. 5) recruiting to expedite infra hires. we'll follow up with a short email and link to action items.

[13:30] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., 'Dedicated' -> 'Ded', 'KV cache' -> 'K-V cash'), small overlaps, filler words, and some proper nouns slightly off in automated transcription.
